# Review: Aeration Blower Control Narrative (WWTP Upgrade)

**Recommendation: do not issue this to the contractor.** It has six critical defects. Items 2 and 5 contradict each other, and as written the blowers will stage off as soon as they reach setpoint. Item 3 shuts off aeration on a common instrument fault. Item 6 restarts all blowers at the same time after an outage. The document also lacks most of the template: states, sequences, alarms, abnormal handling, operator interface, requirement IDs and open items. Return it to the consultant with the findings below.

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | Items 2 and 5 | **Critical.** Units and values conflict. 7.5 psig is about 207.6 inH2O, but staging uses 160/165 inH2O (about 5.78/5.96 psig). When the blowers hold setpoint, header pressure is always above the stage-off value, so the stage-off condition is always true. Blowers will stage off repeatedly and the system will hunt. Stage-on happens only after pressure has collapsed about 23% below setpoint. | Use one pressure unit (psig) everywhere. Remove the absolute stage-on and stage-off pressures. Use the capacity-based staging in R-05, with values from the setpoint list. |
| R-02 | Item 2 | **Critical.** "Fixed setpoint" contradicts "most-open-valve logic resets the setpoint." The contractor cannot implement both. | State that MOV logic resets the PIC-920 setpoint between SP-HDR-MIN and SP-HDR-MAX. SP-HDR-INIT is the setpoint used at start and after MOV is disabled. |
| R-03 | Item 3 | **Critical.** Closing the air valve on DO signal loss stops aeration and mixing in that basin. That risks septic conditions, solids deposition, diffuser fouling and a permit excursion. Over-aeration only costs energy. If several probes fail together, for example from a shared analyzer or power fault, all valves close and the blowers deadhead into surge (R-06). "Loss of DO signal" is also undefined. | Define bad PV as any of: bad quality, out of range, or probe in maintenance/cleaning mode. On bad PV, hold the AIC output at the last good value for DO-BADPV-HOLD, then drive FCV-91x to POS-FALLBACK. Raise an alarm. Return to AUTO only when the operator selects it. |
| R-04 | Item 6 | **Critical.** Restarting all blowers at the same time causes combined inrush on the utility or generator, possible restart of a coasting rotor, surge on an unloaded header, and unexpected starts with personnel present. | Make auto-restart operator-selectable per blower, defaulting to ENABLED. After power is restored, wait PWR-STABLE-DLY. Restart only blowers that were running and are not tripped or locked out. Start them one at a time through the normal start sequence, at RESTART-STAGGER intervals, each after ZERO-SPD-DLY from power loss. Restart DO loops in AUTO from POS-FALLBACK. Restart MOV logic only after all restarts complete. Owner operations and electrical must confirm (OI-03). |
| R-05 | Item 5 | **Critical.** Header pressure is the controlled variable, so it says nothing about whether the blowers have spare capacity. Staging must use capacity. There are also no minimum run or off timers, no stage-off delay, no lead/lag rotation, and the deadband is too narrow. | Stage on when every running blower is at or above its capacity limit (IGV at or above IGV-MAX) AND PIT-920 is below the PIC-920 setpoint by more than DP-STAGE-ON for STAGE-ON-DLY. Stage off when every running blower is at or below IGV-MIN for STAGE-OFF-DLY AND the remaining blowers can carry the load. Apply MIN-RUN and MIN-OFF. Rotate the lead blower on RUN-HR-ROTATE, or when the operator selects it. Freeze MOV reset during staging. |
| R-06 | Whole document | **Critical.** There is no surge protection. Multistage centrifugal blowers need a blow-off valve, or a minimum IGV position with a surge line. There is no protection against all FCVs closing, and no high header pressure protection. | Add blow-off valve tags and a surge-avoidance requirement from the vendor surge map. Add a minimum header flow, or block FCV closure below POS-MIN while any blower runs. Add PIT-920 high alarm and trip rows to the C&E (see below). |
| R-07 | Item 7 | **Major.** Only one trip is listed, with no tag, value, delay, latch or reset. Common protections are missing: motor winding and bearing temperature, discharge temperature, surge, motor overload, and inlet filter dP alarm. | Use the C&E rows below. Confirm the trip list and values with the blower vendor (OI-02). |
| R-08 | Item 4 | **Major.** The discharge valve has no tag or limit switch. There is no blow-off-open, trip-clear, or lockout-clear permissive, and no check valve is mentioned. Starting with the discharge valve open into a live header needs a check valve and an open blow-off to avoid surge. | Start permissives: ZSC-931/932/933 (IGV closed), discharge valve open limit switch, blow-off valve open, no active trip, local/remote in REMOTE, MIN-OFF elapsed. Add the tags to the index. |
| R-09 | Item 1 | **Major.** There are no air flow meters, so DO acts directly on the valve. There is no minimum valve position for mixing and no out-of-service basin handling. | Confirm whether FIT-911 to 914 exist (OI-01). If they do, cascade AIC-90x to FIC-91x. Clamp FCV output at or above POS-MIN while the basin is in service. A basin in OUT OF SERVICE closes its FCV and is excluded from MOV. |
| R-10 | Item 2 | **Major.** MOV logic has no deadband, reset interval, step size, clamps, or rule for valves in MANUAL or bad PV. | Exclude valves in MANUAL, bad PV, or out of service from MOV selection. Reset the setpoint by MOV-STEP every MOV-INT when the most open valve is outside MOV-TARGET ± MOV-DB. Clamp the setpoint to SP-HDR-MIN/MAX. If no valve qualifies, hold the setpoint and alarm. |
| R-11 | Whole document | **Major.** No ISA-106 states or modes are defined. | Add state tables. Blower: OFF, STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING, TRIPPED, LOCKED OUT. Basin: IN SERVICE, OUT OF SERVICE. System: AUTO STAGING, MANUAL STAGING. Give permissives, initiator, allowed exits and automation level for each. |
| R-12 | Whole document | **Major.** There are no start or stop sequences, and no timeouts or failure responses. | Add step tables (Step, Action, Transition, Timeout, Failure response) for blower start and normal stop. Example: open blow-off, start motor, reach speed within START-TO, ramp IGV, close blow-off. |
| R-13 | Whole document | **Major.** Abnormal handling is incomplete. Comms loss between the PLC and blower panels is not covered. Fail positions of FCVs, IGVs and blow-off valves are not stated. Bad PIT-920 is not covered. | Comms loss: blower holds its last IGV position, the panel stays in local pressure control, and an alarm is raised. Bad PIT-920: freeze IGV outputs and staging, then alarm. Fail positions: FCV fail open or last (OI-04), blow-off fail open. |
| R-14 | Whole document | **Major.** No alarms are listed. | Add alarms with responses: DO low/high per basin, DO bad PV, PIT-920 low/high/bad, MOV no valid valve, blower trip, start failure, comms loss, all blowers at max. Rationalize them per ISA-18.2. |
| R-15 | Whole document | **Major.** There is no operator interface section. | Define what the operator sees and can change: DO setpoint per basin, basin in/out of service, lead blower selection, auto-restart enable, auto/manual staging, trip reset. Operations must sign off. |
| R-16 | Items 1, 2, 5 | **Doc.** Setpoints are written in prose (2.0 mg/L, 7.5 psig, 85%, 160/165 inH2O, 2 min). | Move all values to the setpoint list below and refer to them by ID. |
| R-17 | Whole document | **Doc.** No requirement IDs or test methods. | Number each requirement FR-AER-NNN and give a FAT/SAT test method for each. |
| R-18 | Items 2, 4, 7 | **Doc.** B-1/2/3 are not instrument-index tags. The discharge valve, blow-off valve and vibration transmitters have no tags. | Use project tags from the instrument index for all blowers, valves and transmitters. |
| R-19 | Whole document | **Doc.** There is no purpose or boundary section and no interface to the blower vendor control panels. | State the module scope. State the split between the plant PLC and the vendor panel: who controls IGVs and who owns the trips. |
| R-20 | Whole document | **Doc.** There is no SIS statement and no open items list. | State "No SIF identified; confirm at PHA." Add the open items below. |
| R-21 | Items 2, 3, 6 | **Doc.** The wording is ambiguous ("maintain," "loss," "restart automatically"). | Apply the STE pass after the engineering content is settled. |

## Proposed setpoint list

| ID | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| SP-DO | 2.0 | mg/L | From narrative |
| SP-HDR-INIT | 7.5 | psig | From narrative, confirm |
| SP-HDR-MIN | 6.0 | psig | Provisional, confirm from system curve |
| SP-HDR-MAX | 8.0 | psig | Provisional, confirm from blower and diffuser rating |
| MOV-TARGET | 85 | % open | From narrative |
| MOV-DB | 5 | % | Provisional, confirm |
| MOV-STEP | 0.05 | psi | Provisional, confirm |
| MOV-INT | 2 | min | Provisional, confirm |
| DP-STAGE-ON | 0.3 | psi | Provisional, confirm |
| STAGE-ON-DLY | 2 | min | From narrative (reused) |
| STAGE-OFF-DLY | 10 | min | Provisional, confirm |
| IGV-MAX / IGV-MIN | 95 / 20 | % | Provisional, confirm from vendor surge map |
| MIN-RUN / MIN-OFF | 30 / 15 | min | Provisional, confirm with motor vendor |
| RUN-HR-ROTATE | 168 | h | Provisional, confirm with operations |
| POS-MIN | 15 | % open | Provisional, confirm from mixing requirement |
| POS-FALLBACK | Last good output, or 50 | % open | Provisional, confirm |
| DO-BADPV-HOLD | 5 | min | Provisional, confirm |
| PWR-STABLE-DLY | 10 | s | Provisional, confirm with electrical |
| ZERO-SPD-DLY | 60 | s | Provisional, confirm with vendor rundown time |
| RESTART-STAGGER | 30 | s | Provisional, confirm with electrical |
| START-TO | 30 | s | Provisional, confirm with vendor |
| VIB-ALM / VIB-TRIP | 0.30 / 0.50 | in/s pk | Provisional, confirm with vendor |
| VIB-TRIP-DLY | 5 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| PIT-920 HI / HI-HI | SP-HDR-MAX + 0.5 / + 1.0 | psig | Provisional, confirm |

## Proposed C&E rows (blower trips, per blower)

| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vibration above VIB-TRIP for VIB-TRIP-DLY | Stop blower, open blow-off, close discharge valve, start next available blower if stage-on conditions are true | Latched | Operator reset at local panel after the cause clears |
| Motor winding or bearing high-high temperature | Same as above | Latched | Local reset |
| Discharge high-high temperature | Same as above | Latched | Local reset |
| Surge detected (vendor logic) | Open blow-off. Trip after the vendor-set repeat count. | Blow-off auto-reset; trip latched | Local reset |
| Motor overload / protection relay | Stop blower | Latched | Relay reset, then local reset |
| PIT-920 HI-HI | Stop the last-started blower, open blow-offs | Auto-reset when below HI | None needed; alarm acknowledged |
| Start failure (not at speed within START-TO) | Stop blower, alarm, start next available blower | Latched | HMI reset |

## Open items

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Confirm whether FIT-911 to 914 exist; choose DO→valve or DO→flow cascade | Consultant (process) | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-02 | Provide trip list, values, surge map, IGV limits, rundown time, and PLC/panel control split | Blower vendor via consultant | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-03 | Confirm auto-restart policy, stagger, and generator capacity | Owner operations + electrical engineer | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-04 | Confirm FCV-911 to 914 actuator type and fail position | Consultant (mechanical) | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-05 | Confirm header pressure range and minimum basin airflow for mixing | Consultant (process) | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-06 | Confirm no SIF at PHA | Owner (PHA lead) | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-07 | Operations sign-off on states, prompts and HMI changes | Owner operations | After revised draft |

All due dates are proposals. Adjust them to the contractor issue date.
